Infections have been reported in Thailand, the Philippines, Pakistan, and India, with cases in southern United States; Russia has no registered natural occurrences, though Pakistan and India lie nearest to its borders. When contaminated water enters the nose, the amoeba migrates along the olfactory nerve to the brain, triggering severe inflammation and destruction of neural tissue. It adheres to brain cells, releasing enzymes and toxins that dissolve membranes, and the ensuing inflammatory response exacerbates brain edema. The disease progresses rapidly; incubation is about 2–3 days. Most infections are fatal; the maximum time from infection to death is 24 days, with an average under 18 days. These remarks were noted by biologist Dmitry Fedorov.
